stories.headline: Trump unveils America.gov as AI-powered hub for passports, Medicare, and more
stories.summary: President Trump signed an executive order Tuesday launching America.gov, an AI chatbot that searches tens of thousands of federal pages so citizens can ask how to renew a passport, pick a Medicare plan, or chase veterans benefits in one place. U.S. Chief Design Officer Joe Gebbia said forms and status tracking should arrive by 2027, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said first-passport applications will move onto the site then — including user-uploaded photos instead of drugstore shots. Trump framed it as treating people’s time as if it matters, comparing the interface to Grok, Gemini, or ChatGPT.

stories.headline: ICE confusion ignites MAGA backlash after pullback guidance on non-criminal arrests
stories.summary: Reported verbal guidance telling some ICE offices to ease off arrests of illegal immigrants without criminal records sparked a sharp MAGA backlash before the administration walked it back within hours. Trump told Fox there was no change to a “worst first” posture that still leaves no one off the table, while Mass Deportation Coalition’s Mike Howell said mixed DHS messaging — including a Mullin tweet about skipping Kansas worksite ops — would have drawn impeachment calls under a Democrat. CIS’s Mark Krikorian urged the White House to get interior and worksite enforcement signals straight ahead of the midterms.

stories.headline: CNN, Politico, and MS NOW ask court to keep blocking Trump’s White House press ban
stories.summary: CNN, Politico, and MS NOW asked a federal judge for a preliminary injunction extending White House access beyond an Oct. 8 temporary restraining order, arguing the administration has unpredictably reimposed elements of the Sept. 19 ban — including barring CNN from Air Force One and pool duties. Attorney Theodore Boutrous called the ban viewpoint retaliation; AG Todd Blanche insisted access is a privilege and defended keeping CNN off the president’s plane. Judge Timothy Kelly has already signaled due-process skepticism of the sudden ouster.

stories.headline: Trump says he’ll rebrand AI as ‘super intelligence’ in all U.S. government documents
stories.summary: At the America.gov launch Tuesday, President Trump said he would sign an executive order making “super intelligence,” or SI, the official U.S. government name for artificial intelligence — arguing “artificial” undersells the technology. After lunch with Zuckerberg, Jensen Huang, and Elon Musk, he again pushed industry self-regulation and dismissed existential-risk warnings from Anthropic and OpenAI as a “hoax,” saying he will not stifle growth he compares to the industrial revolution.

stories.headline: America.gov chatbot runs on Google Gemini and Elon Musk’s Grok, Gebbia says
stories.summary: U.S. Chief Design Officer Joe Gebbia told CNBC that the new America.gov chatbot is powered behind the scenes by Google’s Gemini and Elon Musk’s Grok. Google published a partner note saying Gemini will help more than 100 million people reach public resources faster; SpaceXAI/xAI did not comment. Gebbia said the tool scans roughly 29,000 government sites so answers stay tied to official sources rather than stale third-party pages — a notable Grok footprint inside a Trump digital-front-door project.

stories.headline: Apple targeting 6–8 million iPhone Duo units for 2026 as yields hover near 60%
stories.summary: Jiemian News supply-chain sourcing, relayed by 9to5Mac, says Apple’s 2026 stocking target for the foldable iPhone Duo is about 6–8 million units — far below the 20–30 million typical for a Pro/Pro Max cycle — while Foxconn final-assembly yields sit just over 60%. Suppliers think mature yields could take another six months or more, and Apple so far will not loosen quality bars that keep early output tight ahead of Oct. 16 pre-orders and the $1,999 starting price.

stories.headline: Rare clearance: medium black Apple Watch Ultra 3 configs fall up to ~$200
stories.summary: With Ultra 4 shipping, Amazon is clearing prior-gen black Apple Watch Ultra 3 kits — including hard-to-find medium sizes — with the Milanese Loop large config near $200 off its $899 list and medium Alpine/Milanese and small Trail options around $100 off. Ultra 4 GPS+Cellular 49mm also shows light launch discounts near $780. Useful for readers who want Ultra toughness without paying new-gen sticker.

stories.headline: Grok 4.7 goes live on Amazon Bedrock with 500K context and four reasoning tiers
stories.summary: AWS added xAI’s Grok 4.7 to Amazon Bedrock with a 500K-token context window, text/image input, and low/medium/high/xhigh reasoning-effort profiles. Artificial Analysis figures cited by AWS show gains versus Grok 4.6 on Intelligence and Coding Agent indexes, with average output tokens per task roughly doubling to ~81K — pitched for long-running coding agents and knowledge work without leaving the Bedrock control plane.

stories.headline: SpaceXAI launches Team Bots — shared Grok teammates with plugins and memory
stories.summary: SpaceXAI opened a public beta of Team Bots for Teams and Enterprise plans: role-based shared Grok agents that combine shared context, plugins (Salesforce, Notion, GitHub), credentials, and memories while keeping each employee’s private chat separate. Internal engineering bots wired to Notion, Linear, Datadog, and Cursor allegedly helped a five-person team ship 100+ PRs a day; bots can also sit in Slack. Pre-built sales, PM, marketing, and data templates ship with the beta.

stories.headline: Five Finger Death Punch lands 18th Mainstream Rock No. 1 with “Eye Of The Storm”
stories.summary: Five Finger Death Punch’s “Eye Of The Storm,” the lead single from Legacy, hit No. 1 on Billboard’s Mainstream Rock Airplay chart — the band’s 18th chart-topper and an extension of their record consecutive-No.-1 streak. Fresh RIAA metal includes Gold for “Welcome to the Circus” and “Darkness Settles In,” Platinum for “Jekyll and Hyde” and “Wash It All Away,” and double Platinum for “A Little Bit Off,” as the 20th Anniversary World Tour rolls toward an early-2027 UK/EU leg with Lamb of God.

stories.headline: Jets notebook: Geno Smith under pressure sparks confidence; run game still to fix
stories.summary: After a 31–24 loss in Detroit, Aaron Glenn said Geno Smith’s poise under pressure — 11-of-12 for 147 yards when pressured, 321 yards and 3 TDs overall — gives the offense something to build on heading to Chicago. Glenn framed Week 4 as a “race to improve,” especially the run game that has stalled since the Titans opener, while Breece Hall (thigh) and Dylan Parham (knee) await Wednesday injury updates; Jordan Meredith already slid in at guard.

stories.headline: Dubas: Bryan Rust to IR, Lizotte’s Tuesday skate may decide opener status
stories.summary: In his start-of-season presser, Penguins GM Kyle Dubas said Bryan Rust is headed to IR week-to-week with an upper-body injury, Ryan Graves remains out indefinitely after knee work, and Blake Lizotte’s big Tuesday practice will decide Wednesday’s Flyers opener availability. Dubas called 2026-27 “pivotal” for closing a 15-point Metro gap on Carolina, kept Crosby talks as an open back-and-forth, shut down Malkin extension chatter, and said Murashov effectively won the crease last spring in the AHL.

stories.headline: Missouri man pleads guilty to shooting and torching Tesla Cybertruck at KC dealership
stories.summary: Kevin Harkins, 28, of Barnhart, Missouri, pleaded guilty in federal court to malicious destruction of property by arson and possessing an unregistered destructive device after a Feb. 13, 2025 attack on the Kansas City Tesla Center. Court papers say a Cybertruck was shot about nine times and set on fire, a Model Y took seven hood hits, and an unbroken Molotov cocktail was recovered; the burned Cybertruck had an $81,985 sale price. He faces a five-year mandatory minimum on the arson count.

stories.headline: 34 video-game LEGO sets retiring Dec. 31 — Mario, Sonic, Minecraft, Horizon, Fortnite
stories.summary: Brick Fanatics’ year-end retirement wave, tallied by VGC, includes 34 video-game LEGO sets spanning Super Mario, Animal Crossing, Fortnite, Horizon, Sonic, and a long Minecraft list, plus the exclusive Arcade Machine (40805). Once stock sells through after Dec. 31, LEGO stops production and secondary-market prices usually jump — a last clean window for collectors before the PlayStation and other October arrivals dominate shelves.
